To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Screening for AAA in males and females aged 65 to 69 reduces AAA rupture and death, and is cost-effective.

screening for AAA reduces the incidence of ruptured AAA and AAA-attributed death in men ages 65 to75, that the benefit of screening women is unknown, that targeting ever-smokers maximizes cost-effectiveness, and that screening may generate net savings.
vascular ultrasound screening for asymptotic AAA in males ages 60 to 75 reduces the incidence of ruptured AAA, the rates of emergency surgery, and AAA-attributed mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of algorithms for the analysis of large scale data.
the development of a novel method for the synthesis of 3,4-dihydro-2H-1,3-benzoxazine-2-ones and the evaluation of their antiproliferative activity in vitro.
understanding the role of social capital, and its interaction with other factors, in the health and well-being of individuals and populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
screening for AAA in males ages 66 to 75 is recommended, with a strong recommendation for males ages 66-74, and a weaker recommendation for males ages >75.
vascular ultrasound screening for asymptotic abdominal aortic aneursysm in males and ever-smokers aged 65 to 75 is recommended.
vascular ultrasound screening for AAA in males and females ages 65 to 74, particularly those who have smoked, is effective and cost-effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benefits of screening for AAA outweigh the harms.
screening is effective and cost-effective, but that the benefit is not as great for women as for men.
vascular ultrasound screening is a cost-effective way of reducing AAA-related morbidity and mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of screening for AAA are not gender neutral.
the evidence base for vascular ultrasound screening for AAA is robust, but that the benefit for women remains uncertain.
screening for AAA in women is not supported by evidence and that the evidence is insufficient to recommend screening women for AAA.
